t: The Number of Full Rounds You Have Played — Align Login and Logout to Quarter Boundaries
o: Chess rounds start every 15 minutes on the clock, and a round counts as played only if we were logged in for its ENTIRE span. Example 1: logging in at 09:31 and out at 10:14 misses the 09:30 round (joined after it began) and the 10:00 round (left before it ended), leaving just 09:45-10:00, so the answer is 1. Example 2 crosses midnight: from 21:30 to 03:00 we get 10 full rounds before midnight plus 12 after, totaling 22. The clean mental model is a minute axis 0..1439 where round k occupies [15k, 15k+15): count rounds wholly inside the played interval, extending the axis by one day (1440 minutes) whenever logout is not later than login.
k: Convert times to minutes since midnight; a round [s, s+15) is fully played iff s >= login and s + 15 <= logout on the possibly day-wrapped axis.
Round the login UP to the next quarter boundary and the logout DOWN to the previous one — partial quarters at either end cannot contain a complete round — then divide the distance by 15.
If logout < login the session crossed midnight: add 1440 to the logout before rounding.

a.n: Approach 1: Enumerate All Rounds of the Day
a.i: There are only 96 rounds in a day. For each, test whether it fits completely inside the played interval, trying both its today placement and its next-day placement (+1440) to handle midnight-crossing sessions. Brisk, obviously correct, and immune to rounding subtleties.
s: Parse both times into minutes; if end <= start add 1440 to end (session wraps past midnight).
For each of the 96 round starts k*15, examine placements k*15 and k*15 + 1440.
Count a placement when s >= start and s + 15 <= end.
a.t: O(96 x 2) = O(1) — two placements for each of the 96 daily rounds.

a.i: A partially covered quarter at either end hosts no complete round, so snap the login up to the next multiple of 15 and the logout down to the previous one; every quarter strictly between is fully covered, and the count falls out of one division. Handle the midnight wrap by adding a day to the logout first. Verify with Example 1: 571 -> ceil 585 (09:45); 614 -> floor 600 (10:00); (600-585)/15 = 1.
s: Parse hh:mm into minutes for both times.
If end < start, add 1440 to end.
Set start = ceil(start / 15) * 15 and end = floor(end / 15) * 15.
a.t: O(1) — a handful of integer operations regardless of session length.

w: The ceiling/floor framing is the interview-ready answer; the enumeration version makes a nice sanity check. Classic pitfalls: counting the login quarter as fully played when joining mid-round (that is why Example 1's 09:30 round does not count), forgetting the midnight wrap when logout < login, and boundary off-by-ones — logging in exactly AT a quarter start does cover that round, which ceiling handles automatically. Edge cases: one-minute sessions (answer 0) and sessions ending exactly on a boundary. Follow-up: count rounds touched at least partially (round outward instead), or support arbitrary round lengths.
